subject: SCIENCE
title: Animal Parts at Work
objective: Explain that animal body parts can support different functions.
introduction: A fish steers with fins, a bird flies with wings, and a monkey balances with its tail. How do body parts help different animals?

vocabulary.definition: A living thing with body parts, such as a dog, fish, or bird.
All the parts that make up a person or animal.
The natural place where a plant or animal gets what it needs.

items.prompt: Milo compares a fish fin, a bird wing, and a monkey tail. Which statement is true?

options.text: The same kind of part may have different functions across species.
Every fin helps an animal fly

items.explanation: A body part can support different jobs in different animals. A tail may help balance or signal, and not every winged animal flies.

items.prompt: A fish is swimming past Maxine. Which pair matches a body part to its job?
items.explanation: Fins push against water and help a fish swim. Fins do not make an animal fly, and wings and fur have different jobs.

items.prompt: Milo reads four claims about animal parts. Which statement is NOT true?
items.explanation: Tails can have different jobs, including balance, steering, or signaling, so they do not have only one function. Wings and fins can support the jobs named.

items.prompt: A fish wiggles through a pond. Which body part often helps it swim?
items.explanation: Fins push against water to help the fish move. Fur, antlers, and wings are not the fish parts doing this swimming job.

items.prompt: A monkey uses its tail while moving along a branch. Which body part-and-job pair fits?

options.text: Tails may aid balance or communication

items.explanation: Some tails help an animal balance or send signals. Wings do not help swimming, fins do not help flying, and fur is not a fish steering part.
